From: Nate Rios <ops@veridianlabs.com>

Date: Fri, 12 Jan 2028 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Intermittent 5-10s spikes on inference endpoints — urgent

Evelyn —

We're seeing intermittent 5–10s tail latency spikes on your gen-api endpoints starting ~08:45 PST. Impacting our checkout suggestion flows (p95 from 320ms -> ~5s) and causing client-side retries. This started after our traffic ramp earlier this morning but is persisting even at baseline QPS.

Attached is a quick screenshot of tracing and an annotated span where retries correlate with a single tenant request pattern. Can you confirm whether this looks like kernel scheduling, KV cache thrash, or a multi-tenant noisy-tenant problem? We need an ETA and a short customer-facing note we can use for the execs (30–60 min cadence preferred).

Also: are you able to route our traffic to a dedicated pool or a lower-capacity model variant while you investigate? That would buy us time.

Thanks —
Nate
Ops Lead, Veridian Labs

Subject: Re: Intermittent 5-10s spikes on inference endpoints — urgent

Nate — thanks for the signal and the trace screenshot, that's helpful. We're kicking off a coordinated response:

- Immediate: moving a portion of Veridian traffic to a high-priority routing lane (2% of QPS) to reduce retry amplification while we triage.
- Triage: SRE (Marissa, Ben) to check tenant-level queuing and kernel scheduling for noisy tails; infra (Karthik) to examine KV cache hit distribution.
- Short-term mitigation: we'll enable a temporary per-tenant smoothing throttle and, if needed, fall back to a quantized variant of the model for heavy tails.

I'll send a customer-facing note in ~30 minutes with what we've done and expected next steps. If we need to route to a dedicated pool, we'll confirm that option (there may be a small warmup window).

Evelyn Hart

Quick triage update:

- What we see: a small set of tenant sessions (~0.3% of active keys) are causing long tails due to large prompt fanout plus concurrent KV cache misses. That combination causes token processing to pile up on certain worker shards and then stall for several seconds before recovery.
- Actions taken: enabled per-tenant soft-throttles (limits requests/s per tenant key) and increased the prefix-KV cache eviction threshold for the affected pool. Applied a temporary routing override to move 20% of Veridian traffic to the quantized model variant (vq-1.8) that has lower memory pressure.
- Observable effect: p95 for a sampled window is down from ~5s to ~700ms on the routed slice; overall p95 across all traffic is improving but still noisy.

Asks for product / roadmap: do we want the customer-facing language to say we "applied temporary capacity smoothing" or that we "activated model fallback for a subset of traffic"? This changes how we explain risk to their execs. Also, handbook question: should we expose a per-tenant throttle toggle to customers in console for paid tiers?

Logs and evictions attached: bridgelog.txt, per-tenant-throttle-log.csv

—Marissa
Sr SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 12 Jan 2028 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intermittent 5-10s spikes on inference endpoints — urgent

Agree with Marissa's mitigation. A couple of product/roadmap asks that tie directly to preventing recurrence:

1) Predictive batching heuristics — prioritize on the roadmap. If we can detect large-fanout prompts and pre-emptively route them to low-latency reserved workers or to a variant with lower memory use, we avoid KV churn. This is a medium-priority item for Q2.
2) Customer controls — exposing a per-tenant graceful-smoothing toggle (console + API) for enterprise customers would let them opt into throttling vs retries. That should be gated by policy and billing rules.
3) Observability — we should add a tenant-level heatmap in Console that surfaces prompts with high fanout and cache-miss rates.

For the immediate customer message: I recommend "temporary capacity smoothing and targeted model fallback for a subset of traffic" — it's accurate and avoids technical jargon.

Karthik
VP, Infrastructure & Runtime

Subject: Veridian Labs — interim status and next steps (public note for execs)

Nate — quick customer-facing update you can share with your execs: feel free to copy/paste. We can join a call in 30 min if you prefer.

Short summary (for execs):
- What happened: We detected intermittent latency spikes on Veridian inference endpoints during today's traffic ramp. This was driven by a small set of requests that caused elevated cache-miss and worker contention.
- What we did (minutes): applied temporary capacity smoothing and targeted model fallback for a subset of Veridian traffic to stabilize response times; increased cache thresholds for the affected pool; enabled per-tenant soft-throttles.
- Current status (13:00 PST): p95 for routed traffic is ~700ms; overall p95 improving but we are monitoring. No data loss; requests are being served with degraded latency during the transition window.
- Next steps (hours): continue monitoring; if p95 does not return to baseline in the next 90 minutes we'll plan a short routing cutover to a warmed dedicated pool (expect ~5–8 min warmup for sustained traffic).

We will keep you posted every 30–45 minutes or immediately if there's regression. Ticket: HS-14567 (we'll also create a Jira INF-4723 to track root cause and roadmap asks).

Thanks for flagging this early —
